mechanism: During night and morning, a shallow stable boundary layer traps local respiration and emissions, producing a distinct high-CO2 diurnal phase.
activation_condition: when hour_of_day is night or morning
failure_condition: when strong synoptic mixing or frontal passage breaks the stable layer, or outside night/morning hours
retrieval_action: Retrieve historical segments from the same hour-of-day category and weight them more heavily.
reason: CO2 at a roof station has a strong diurnal cycle driven by boundary-layer stability; matching the time of day avoids mixing daytime and nighttime regimes.
expected_effect: The retrieved future will match the correct diurnal phase of CO2 accumulation and boundary-layer state.

mechanism: Winter roof-level CO2 is typically elevated and more variable because combustion emissions increase and vertical mixing is often weaker.
failure_condition: when an unusual warm, windy period creates summer-like ventilation despite the calendar season
retrieval_action: Restrict historical retrieval mainly to winter segments, or strongly prefer the same season.
reason: Seasonal CO2 level and variance differ strongly; winter segments are more predictive of winter future dynamics than summer or transition-season segments.
expected_effect: The retrieved future will have a realistic high winter baseline and reduced-mixing dynamics.

mechanism: On workday mornings, traffic and heating emissions create a sharp CO2 rise that is absent or weaker on non-working days.
activation_condition: when working_day is workday AND hour_of_day is morning
failure_condition: when a public holiday or shutdown makes a weekday behave like a non-working day, or when morning wind rapidly disperses emissions
retrieval_action: Retrieve historical workday morning segments, preferring the same working-day category and hour-of-day category.
reason: Workday schedules impose a weekly cycle on urban CO2, so matching both working-day status and hour-of-day captures the emission-driven morning peak.
expected_effect: The retrieved future will contain the workday morning CO2 ramp rather than a flat weekend morning profile.

mechanism: Non-working middays often have lower and smoother CO2 because traffic and work-related emissions are reduced.
activation_condition: when working_day is non_working AND hour_of_day is midday
failure_condition: when local leisure, residential heating, or atmospheric stagnation creates workday-like CO2 levels on a non-working day
retrieval_action: Retrieve historical non-working midday segments, preferring the same working-day category and hour-of-day category.
reason: The weekly emission cycle matters for roof-level CO2; non-working middays have a distinct lower-emission signature compared with workday middays.
expected_effect: The retrieved future will have a lower, less workday-influenced CO2 profile.

mechanism: High recent volatility indicates active local emission events or variable mixing, and future CO2 is likely to remain in a similarly fluctuating regime.
failure_condition: when the high volatility was a short isolated pulse and the system returns quickly to calm conditions
retrieval_action: Retrieve historical segments with similarly high recent volatility rather than smooth periods.
reason: CO2 variability is regime-dependent; matching volatility helps the retriever select futures with compatible local source or mixing behavior.
expected_effect: The retrieved future will reflect the correct fluctuation amplitude and unstable regime rather than underestimating variability.

mechanism: A strong recent slope during morning often reflects the characteristic post-sunrise CO2 ramp from traffic and boundary-layer development.
activation_condition: when recent_slope_magnitude is high AND hour_of_day is morning
failure_condition: when the steep slope is caused by a short local plume rather than the regular morning transition
retrieval_action: Retrieve historical morning segments with similarly high recent slope magnitude and prefer the same hour-of-day category.
reason: The morning ramp has a characteristic slope; matching both slope magnitude and time of day selects historical transitions with similar dynamics.
expected_effect: The retrieved future will capture the continuation or typical shape of the morning CO2 ramp.

mechanism: High recent difference magnitude indicates jumpy CO2 from intermittent local sources or abrupt mixing changes, and future may continue to show sharp short-term movements.
failure_condition: when the large differences were a one-time sensor-ventilation fluctuation and subsequent behavior is smooth
retrieval_action: Retrieve historical segments with similarly high recent difference magnitude rather than smoothly varying segments.
reason: Short-term differences capture high-frequency local CO2 forcing; matching this feature selects futures with similar intermittent emission or mixing behavior.
expected_effect: The retrieved future will preserve the correct magnitude of short-term CO2 jumps instead of smoothing them away.
